question: Does the August vision recipe learn the new bench task from camera pixels, on the simulator scene that now has the measured joint map and the calibrated camera?
measure: Successes out of 30 on held-out cube positions (10 new positions, 3 tries each), the number of safety frames, and the same count with the camera image blacked out. A good result is high success, zero safety frames, and a collapse to 0 with a black image.
outcome: Normal position 3/3, held-out 27/30, zero safety frames in all 33 rollouts. With a black image 0/3 and 0/30. All 3 failures were one cube position (6 mm left and 6 mm short), where the cube was lifted 28 mm without a strict grasp.
setup:
A policy is the network that drives the arm. Here it is the vision policy from August: it sees only the wrist camera image (256x256) and the arm's joint readings, never the cube position. It outputs a chunk of 90 actions at a time (H90), so it gets a fresh look every 90 steps of the 480-step episode.

The teacher is a hand-written script that solves the task using the true cube position. The policy is trained to copy the teacher's episodes.

Held-out means cube positions the policy never saw in training: 10 new positions, 3 tries each, so 30 rollouts (a rollout is one full episode run by the policy in the simulator). Nominal is the normal cube position, 3 tries.

A safety frame is a simulation step where a command broke a safety limit. Zero is the goal. The gripper clamp is a rule from August that clips the gripper command to its allowed range.

The black-image ablation runs the same policy with the camera image replaced by black. If it still succeeds, it was not using the camera. A seed is the random number that fixes the network's starting weights and data order; different seeds can give different results.

What is new: this is the first training run on the bench task (a 20 mm cube on a 2 inch white square, 8.5 inches from the arm base). Everything in August ran on an older task with a wrong joint map and a wrong camera (experiments 20 and 21). The recipe was written down before the run as gates 3 to 5 of the bench plan: 400 teacher-screened training positions (seed 12) and 10 held-out positions (seed 8), all within 10 mm of the square centre; exactly one run, seed 202, 120,000 steps, hidden width 256, batch 64, Adam 1e-3, with the gripper clamp. The plan also says a single run is exploratory, not a claim that the policy is ready.

parts.title: Does the recipe carry over to the bench task?
parts.why: If it learns, head toward the real arm. If not, the plan said to try more data or a second seed before changing the recipe.
parts.did: Ran the pipeline once: screen and capture 400 teacher episodes, train 120,000 steps, then evaluate on the normal position and on the held-out positions.
parts.conclusion: It carried over in one run: 27/30 on new positions with zero safety frames. Final training loss was about 1e-6.

parts.title: Is it really using the camera?
parts.why: In August (experiment 15) a vision policy mostly ignored its image, because the cube never moved. A policy that ignores the image cannot find a cube in a new place.
parts.did: Re-ran both suites with the image replaced by black.
parts.conclusion: Yes. With a black image it scores 0/3 and 0/30 (0 of 33 in all) with 204 and 2055 safety frames. The cube now moves between episodes, so the image is the only place the answer is.

parts.title: What are the three failures?
parts.why: Three failures spread over three positions would mean general unreliability. Three on one position means one hard spot.
parts.conclusion: All three are one held-out position, pose_006, with the cube 6 mm left and 6 mm short of the normal position. The result repeats exactly across the three tries: the cube is lifted 28 mm but with no strict grasp (jaws on opposite faces), so the pickup counts as incomplete, the cube is released and the episode times out.

trust.text: The recipe (data counts, seeds, steps, one run only) was written into the bench plan before the run.
The held-out positions come from a different seed (8) than the training positions (12).
The numbers in the notes match evaluation_summary.json in the run folder.
One training seed. The plan itself calls a single run exploratory.
30 held-out rollouts are 10 positions repeated 3 times, and the repeats are deterministic, so this is closer to 9 of 10 positions than to 27 of 30 independent tries.
Cube positions vary only within 10 mm of the square centre.
Simulation only. The sim rendered a perfect pinhole image while the real lens bends the image, so this policy would need real frames undistorted first. That was not implemented.
No pass bar was registered for the success count, so there is no prediction to mark.

meaning: This was the first real evidence on the bench task, and it said the August recipe transfers once the simulator is calibrated and the cube position is randomized. It did not authorize a real-arm trial: the observation still differed from the real camera (pinhole against a bending lens). That was fixed the next day by rendering the sim through the real lens (experiment 23), with the same recipe.
lesson: With a calibrated sim and randomized cube positions, the August recipe carried over to the new task in one run. And the black-image test is what shows the camera is doing the work.

next.title: Make the sim render through the real lens and repeat the run (experiment 23)
next.why: This policy expects pinhole images; the real camera has strong barrel distortion.

next.title: More data or a second seed before any recipe change
next.why: The plan's stated next lever after a single exploratory run.

log:
**TL;DR:** 27/30 on new cube positions with zero safety frames, and 0/30 with a
black image, so this time it really used the camera.

**Problem.** This was the first real evidence on the bench task. Everything in
August ran on the old task with the wrong arm and camera.

*How we know:* entries 20-21 found the joint map and lens were both wrong. I
didn't know if the August recipe would carry over.

**Experiment.** One run, written down beforehand: 400 screened cube positions
(±10 mm around the task pose), seed 202, 120k steps, the vision policy with the
gripper clip, on the calibrated scene. Test on 10 new positions, 3 tries each,
and again with black images.

*What we hope to learn:* if it learns, head toward the real arm. If not, more
data or a second seed before changing the recipe.

**Outcome.** Normal start 3/3, new positions 27/30, zero safety frames. With
black images, 0/30 and 2,055 bad frames. All 3 failures were one position (6 mm
left and 6 mm short), where it lifted the cube 28 mm without a strict grasp.

- Unlike entry 15, blanking the camera kills it, because the cube actually
  moves now. The image is the only place the answer is.

One catch: the sim rendered a perfect pinhole while the real lens bends the
image, so this policy would need real frames undistorted first. That got fixed
the next day.

**Takeaway:** with a calibrated sim and randomized positions, the August recipe
carried over to the new task in one run.
